#5277. BNB Crypto Drops 8.7% in an Hour as Binance Loses $6.36 Billion to Hackers, and Futures Traders Turn Short: Can BNB Hold Its 200-Day Average?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour after the Binance hack and is lagging Bitcoin, as shorts pile in. Can BNB hold its 200-day EMA at $692?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour on Thursday, October 29, from $744.90 to $680, as hackers drained about $6.36 billion from Binance, the exchange behind the token, in the largest crypto theft on record. The bounce since has been the weakest among the big coins. BNB trades at $702, down 6.2% in 24 hours, with a $92.4 billion market cap and 48.7% below its $1,370 record from October 2025. In futures, traders who bet against it are now paying to keep those bets open.

So why is BNB taking the hack harder than Bitcoin, what happened to it after Binance’s last two security scares, and where are the levels that matter?

If a $6.3B security breach can't completely break $BNB, what will?

The market is testing @BNBCHAIN resilience right now.

Historically, moments of maximum fear can create the best opportunities.

DISCOVER: Meme coin supercycle: Top performers this week

Because it is the coin most tied to Binance itself, and futures traders are now betting on that link. From the 20:00 UTC price on Thursday, BNB is still down 5.6%, more than Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP or Dogecoin.

Large-cap coins since the Binance hack. Source: Binance

The hack itself didn’t touch BNB Chain. TRM Labs’ breakdown lists ten blockchains the attacker drained Binance wallets on, from Ethereum to Polygon, and BNB Chain isn’t among them. What traders are pricing is the exchange: BNB is Binance’s token, so a hit to Binance reads as a hit to BNB.

“The Binance exploit has intensified market-wide selling, with BNB facing the greatest exposure,” Zeus Research analyst Dominick John said. Rick Maeda of Laevitas saw it the other way, calling the drop “quite modest for possibly the largest exchange theft ever.”

The futures market sides with the bears. On OKX:

Put together, that reads as many small accounts buying the dip and fewer, larger traders shorting it. If BNB bounces, those shorts are fuel for a squeeze. If it breaks lower, the crowded longs are.

It fell further at first, then recovered within a month both times. Binance has been here twice before:

This time BNB is 8.7% under its pre-hack price at its worst so far. If it follows either path, there could be another leg down before any recovery.

The comparison traders keep reaching for is FTT, the FTX token that lost almost all its value when the exchange collapsed in November 2022. The difference is the balance sheet. FTX had spent customer money and couldn’t pay it back. Binance says it will cover all losses from this hack, and Tether, Circle and others froze about $2.7 billion of the stolen funds within hours.

Traders haven’t fully relaxed, though. Binance hasn’t said how it will fund the payout, and withdrawals stay shut until the reopening it expects within 48 hours of its Friday morning update.

EXPLORE: CZ Tells Crypto Users to Be “Extra Careful” Online as PHP Vulnerabilities Hit the Code Behind 70% of Websites: Can a Hacked Site Drain Your Wallet?

It is holding by a thin margin. BNB closed Thursday at $698.46, just above its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $692.46, after the hack-hour wick to $680 dipped below it. The 50-day EMA at $733.06 is now overhead.

The four-month chart puts BNB back where it was in late August. It traded between $674.60 and $726 for two weeks before breaking out in early September and running to $809.99 on October 5. Thursday’s drop erased that whole move.

For BNB crypto, the next 48 hours carry more weight than any chart line. A smooth reopening of Binance withdrawals would leave the shorts on the wrong side of a crowded trade. A delay, or any sign Binance is selling BNB to pay for the hack, would put $674.60 in play.

A headline claiming that 1.8 billion XRP moved across the XRP Ledger within 24 hours has revived discussion of a network recovery. The figure hasn't been independently verified for a dated 24-hour period, so treat it as a reported claim, not confirmed evidence of a new trend.

The XRP Ledger handles payments, decentralized exchange transactions and tokenized assets. Payment volumes reflects the network activity, but the number needs context. Large transfers can be exchange custody movements, internal treasury operations or transfers between wallets controlled by the same entity.

None of that necessarily signals fresh investor demand or new capital entering the market.

Recent verified reporting shows why the distinction matters. One October snapshot had daily payment volume jumping to about 137.7 million XRP, still below its 30-day average of roughly 496 million.

Another October reading, around 363.3 million XRP, came with the same caution: a one-day rise did not establish a sustained recovery.

A reading near 1.8 billion XRP usually comes at the end of the week where most of the network activity occurs. The most likely outcome is always the same: high activity by Thursday and Friday and a tubmling on the weekend, with a recovery starting on Monday.

Other indicators help separate real adoption from a passing spike: active addresses, successful payment counts, decentralized-exchange trading, liquidity and how transaction sizes are distributed. Even high transaction counts can mislead when automated activity dominates, as recent investigations into small-value stablecoin payments on XRPL showed.

Network usage and XRP's market price are only indirectly related. More settlement activity doesn't guarantee higher token prices, and speculative buying can lift prices with no matching improvement in usage. Broader market conditions and exchange liquidity matter too.

A verified natural burst of XRP movement could mean renewed engagement with the network. A more convincing signal would be several consecutive days of stronger, widely distributed activity, backed by improving liquidity and sustained user demand, which rarely happens.

Block, Circle and Riot Platforms are set to release their Q3 2026 earnings reports in the first week of November.

Circle's USDC circulation increased to $74.58 billion, but lower reserve returns could pressure earnings.

Block (XYZ), Circle Internet Group (CRCL), and Riot Platforms (RIOT) are three key crypto related stocks to watch this week as they prepare to release Q3 2026 earnings reports in the first week of November.

Investors will be watching how Block’s Bitcoin business, Circle’s USDC growth, and Riot’s mining and AI operations are performing.

On 3 November 3, Block will release its Q3 2026 earnings report, the same day as the U.S. midterm elections. Market analysts expect earnings per share to rise to $0.68 from $0.54 a year earlier. Revenue is also forecast to grow 8.4% to $6.63 billion.

However, Bitcoin revenue is expected to fall 12.2% year over year to approximately $1.73 billion. This shows that Block could earn more overall even as its Bitcoin business brings in less revenue.

Investors will also examine Cash App’s performance. Cash App inflows are expected to rise to $89.47 billion from $78.80 billion. Its gross profit is also forecast to increase to $1.97 billion from $1.62 billion.

Gross payment volume is expected to reach $77.16 billion, compared with $69.28 billion in the previous-year period. These figures will help show whether Block is attracting more payment activity and generating stronger profits from its financial services.

As of now, Block (XYZ) shares are trading near $76.35, up around 17% this year, after recovering from a drop toward $72.50.

Next we’ve Circle Internet Group (CRCL), which is scheduled to release its Q3 earnings report on November 4. Investors will be watching whether growth in its USDC stablecoin can support earnings as interest rates put pressure on its income.

USDC in circulation reached $74.58 billion in Q3, up from $73.3 billion at the end of Q2. This gives Circle more reserves to manage, but lower interest rates could reduce the returns it earns on those funds.

Despite the increase in USDC circulation, analysts expect Circle’s earnings per share to fall around 37% year over year to $0.37–$0.40. Revenue is forecast at $788 million to $796.95 million, while adjusted EBITDA is expected to reach $210.8 million.

Circle shares recently traded near $72.54, down 29% over two months.

Lastly, we have Riot Platforms, which is lined up for its ts Q3 results on November 4, Investors will also watch how Riot expands beyond Bitcoin mining into AI data centres. The company has secured a $573 million credit facility from Morgan Stanley for equipment and development costs.

Analysts expect a quarterly loss of approximately $0.24–$0.34 per share, compared with earnings of $0.26 a year earlier. Revenue is also forecast to fall 10.4% to around $160.39 million–$161.46 million.

Bitcoin mining revenue is expected to drop 29.8% to $112.85 million, even though Riot is forecast to mine 1,628 BTC, up from 1,406 BTC a year earlier. This difference shows how mining revenue depends not only on production but also on Bitcoin prices and mining economics.

Meanwhile, engineering revenue is forecast to increase 55.2% to approximately $29.63 million.

As of now, Riot shares traded between $12.81 and $13.11, down about 36.5% over the past month.

In late October 2026, Zcash (ZEC) reached a key milestone: the coin's price consolidated around $1,280, and its market capitalization hit $21.8 billion. However, the rapid rally was overshadowed by a sharp split within the community.

The trigger of the crisis was not a technical problem but a revolt of large investors over the targeted spending of capital.

Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), the organization that distributes part of the miners' block reward, launched the Zcash Adoption Pool program. The fund directed grants toward the integration of vulnerable groups like refugees without access to banks.

The decision sparked protest from major players, since ZCG's charter allows it to distribute multimillion-dollar budgets bypassing the coinholder vote. The "whale" revolt moved into the practical realm: a major holder under the pseudonym "big z" publicly announced a full sell-off of his ZEC holdings.

According to him, the fund should finance cryptography, not political manifestos.

The local conflict quickly grew into a debate about the nature of decentralized money, which industry heavyweights joined. Developer Sean Bowe published a manifesto on the future of ZCG, in which he called for revising the fund's financing due to the anomalous surge in the ZEC price.

The initiative was unexpectedly supported by legendary investor Naval Ravikant, who laconically snapped that a $50 million cap is more than enough for community grants.

Meanwhile, the fund's activists continue to insist that private money is a "humanitarian imperative" and a public good.

However, Gemini exchange co-founder Tyler Winklevoss harshly challenged this thesis: a commercial network with transaction fees cannot be a public good. Winklevoss compared ZCG's actions to "taxation without representation" and called for leaving the development of Zcash to the free market.

The pressure on the price from the whales' coin sell-off coincided with the launch of direct ZEC deposits on the decentralized Rujira Network on October 29.

After failing to break above $1,390, the price settled in the $1,220–1,245 $range, still well below the all-time high of $1,698 set in late September. The fundamental dispute over who should control Zcash's millions remains open.

#5273. Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying, as Route 2 FI Buys the Dip

Bitcoin news: the Binance hacker holds $1.4B in BTC, 3x this week’s ETF inflows. Will Binance’s buyback help, and can BTC hold $76,500?

Bitcoin news on Friday turned to a warning from trader Route 2 FI, who said the Binance hacker’s $1.4 billion in BTC is more than three times what spot ETFs bought all week, a potential seller hanging over Bitcoin at $77,300.

Arkham’s entity page shows the Binance hacker holding 18,270 BTC worth $1.42 billion and 488,364 ETH worth $1.09 billion across 73 addresses. US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million from Monday to Thursday.

Route 2 FI still likes the setup enough to take a position. The trader expects Binance to recover fully but thinks the hack will push more people toward decentralized exchanges.

Binance would need a couple of months to fill this hole, unless they use other shady tactics to get whole faster.

The hacker has $BTC worth $1.4b and $ETH worth $1b ready to sell. For $BTC, that's more than 3x the $450M that spot ETFs bought all week.

— Route 2 FI (@Route2FI) October 30, 2026

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Holds $79,200 Before the Fed, Coinbase Earnings and a $10.9B Expiry: Which Way Next?

Route 2 FI’s math holds up. Arkham’s Binance Hacker entity shows 18,270 BTC, worth $1.42 billion at Friday’s prices. SoSoValue figures show US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million across four straight days of inflows from October 26 to 29. That makes the hacker’s Bitcoin about 3.2 times a week of ETF demand.

Binance hacker holdings on October 30, 2026 vs spot Bitcoin ETF inflows for October 26 to 29. Sources: Arkham, SoSoValue.

The hacker hasn’t sold any of the Bitcoin yet. The selling so far has been in smaller tokens: Lookonchain tracked the attacker dumping UNI, PEPE, ENA, LINK and others for 70,480 ETH, worth about $158 million.

On the other side, Binance is already buying. The exchange told CoinDesk it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover the losses, $5 billion of it already held in the same tokens the attackers took, and is buying the rest on exchanges and over the counter. About $3 billion of the stolen funds is frozen and doesn’t need replacing.

“Binance’s SAFU fund and Binance’s holdings include a large amount of assets such as BTC and ETH. We are currently buying, through OTC and on-exchange, all the stolen altcoins in fully matching amounts.”

That matters for Bitcoin. If Binance already holds enough BTC to cover customers, its buying lands mostly on altcoins, which leaves the hacker’s 18,270 BTC as a seller without a matching buyer.

Route 2 FI pointed to the Bybit hack as the template. Attackers took about $1.4 billion in ether from Bybit on February 21, 2025, and the exchange replaced it within days through loans, deposits and market purchases.

The buyback gave prices only a short lift. Measured from the February 20, 2025 close on Binance:

Ethereum bounced while Bybit bought, then lost more than a third of its value within three weeks. The broader market sold off over that stretch for reasons beyond the hack, so the table shows that buyback demand fades fast. It doesn’t show that the hack caused the slide.

Route 2 FI also argued that the hack, coming a year after the October 10, 2025 crash, gives traders another reason to keep less money on centralized exchanges. Binance paid out more than $283 million in compensation after that crash, when some assets lost their pegs on its platform.

The trader cited the jump in Hyperliquid’s HYPE token as proof. The timing doesn’t fit, though. HYPE rose from $79.38 to a $97.09 high between 10:00 and 16:00 UTC on Thursday, after ICE and Trade.xyz announced plans for a regulated US perpetuals venue on Hyperliquid. That was about ten hours before the Binance drain began at 20:04 UTC.

After the hack, HYPE fell to $88.55 and trades at $90.83.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Whale Sends $35M to Coinbase at a $15M Loss as October Turns Red: What Moves BTC Next?

The setup Route 2 FI is buying is easy to see on the daily chart since early August. Bitcoin’s $76,500 low on Friday stopped $35 above its 200-day EMA at $76,465, a line it has closed above every day since the late-August breakout. BTC trades at $77,326, down 3.5% in 24 hours.

August 2 to October 30, 2026: BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

The last time Bitcoin tested the 200-day line, in mid-September, it held at $74,968 and climbed to $87,395 within a week. A trader buying here has a clear line to be wrong at.

For Bitcoin news over the coming week, two things decide which row plays out: whether Binance reopens withdrawals on schedule, and whether the hacker’s Bitcoin starts to move.

#5272. Japan’s Inflation Signal Matters More To XRP Than The Rate

Home » Trendsetter News » Japan’s Inflation Signal Matters More To XRP Than The Rate

A shift in the Bank of Japan’s inflation language could rattle crypto markets even without a rate hike.

A change in the Bank of Japan’s inflation language could unsettle crypto markets even without an interest-rate increase, prominent crypto commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her video. Her focus is whether policymakers declare that underlying inflation has reached their 2% target—a signal she says could point toward further tightening.

Dr. Stevenson says the central bank has not made that declaration since adopting the target in 2013.

She cites a Bloomberg survey in which no economists expected an immediate hike, making the bank’s wording, rather than its rate decision alone, the potential surprise.

The transmission mechanism is the yen carry trade: investors borrow in Japan’s low-interest-rate currency to buy higher-returning assets elsewhere. Higher Japanese borrowing costs can squeeze those positions, while a stronger yen makes repayment more expensive for investors holding dollar-denominated assets.

Dr. Stevenson points to August 5, 2024, when Japanese stocks fell more than 12% and crypto also sold off. The Bank of Japan had raised its policy rate to around 0.25% several days earlier.

She presents forced selling from carry-trade unwinds as the central explanation. That is the video’s interpretation, rather than evidence that Japanese policy alone caused the entire decline.

There is another possible channel. Japan holds more than $1 trillion in U.S. Treasuries, according to the episode; more attractive domestic yields could encourage Japanese investors to bring money home. Treasury selling could put upward pressure on U.S. yields, although that outcome is not automatic.

For XRP, Stevenson separates near-term market pressure from longer-term payments activity. A rapid yen appreciation could accompany selling across crypto, regardless of developments specific to XRP.

Her longer-term argument centers on SBI’s involvement with XRP, including payments through SBI Remit and lending services. She suggests that growing blockchain-based transfers between Japan and the United States could create demand for cross-currency settlement.

That remains a potential use case, not a demonstrated link between Japanese rate increases and XRP demand. More stablecoin activity does not necessarily require XRP.

Solana price faces continued selling pressure as a large whale deposits 1.49 million SOL worth nearly $148.77 million into exchanges.

Solana price is struggling to reclaim the $100 mark as selling pressure continues to weigh on the cryptocurrency. Large whale transfers to exchanges, persistent withdrawals from spot Solana ETFs and weakening technical momentum are creating a challenging environment for buyers. The token has also extended its losing streak, raising concerns about whether the current correction could deepen.

Three factors are putting pressure on SOL and could determine whether it manages to recover or faces another leg lower.

Large-scale whale activity is one of the latest concerns for Solana investors. On-chain data shared by Lookonchain shows that an unidentified whale deposited approximately 1.49 million SOL, worth around $148.77 million, into multiple cryptocurrency exchanges over the past 10 days.

Institutional investment flows are providing another challenge for Solana. US-listed spot Solana ETFs recorded approximately $71.47 million in net outflows last week, marking their largest weekly withdrawals since launch.

Sustained outflows can weaken the demand supporting an asset, particularly when broader market conditions are already negative. A return to consistent inflows could help stabilize sentiment, but continued withdrawals may leave the token vulnerable to further selling.

However, the $88.42 area remains the key downside support. A decisive break below this zone could expose the next major support near $78.35. The daily RSI is approaching oversold territory, but the negative MACD suggests bearish momentum has not yet clearly reversed.

Solana’s recovery depends on whether buyers can absorb the selling pressure from large holders and restore demand through institutional investment. A move above $100 would be an early positive signal, followed by the $103–$104 resistance zone.

On the other hand, continued whale deposits and ETF outflows could keep SOL under pressure. A breakdown below $88.42 would increase the risk of a deeper correction toward $78.35.

#5267. Binance Hack Exposes Never-Before-Seen Money Laundering Tactics

Home » Crypto Market News » Binance Hack Exposes Never-Before-Seen Money Laundering Tactics

The $6.4 billion theft has triggered an unusual automated laundering operation as investigators work to trace the stolen funds.

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis has identified a “never-seen-before” money-laundering pattern in the aftermath of the $6.4 billion Binance hack. Thousands of transactions conducted within a short period suggest the attackers are using automation to obscure the trail.

Chainalysis calls the theft the largest in crypto history and attributes it to North Korean group TraderTraitor. About $2.8 billion has been frozen so far, while the attackers continue attempts to move the remaining assets.

According to a Chainalysis report, rather than simply moving the funds onward, the attackers repeatedly circulate them among addresses, often sending them back to addresses involved earlier in the sequence.

Investigators have also identified a recurring pattern involving TRON (TRX). Many involved addresses first receive exactly 1 TRX before receiving additional funds and forwarding them elsewhere.

Chainalysis believes these repeated sequences point to a programmatic operation rather than manual transfers. The thousands of transactions suggest automation is being used to distribute the stolen assets and complicate blockchain tracing.

Our investigators are observing never-seen-before laundering patterns with the stolen funds from the Binance exploit. Thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation to obscure the trail of funds. Rather than simply moving funds onward,… pic.twitter.com/Uhu3dbxDqh

The attack against Binance began around 4:20 p.m. Eastern Time on October 29, when unauthorized transfers started draining Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains.

On Ethereum, the attacker used an operational wallet funded through Tornado Cash to submit valid signed authorizations. These permissions allowed a Binance hot wallet to execute attacker-deployed code, which was subsequently used to transfer its assets into wallets controlled by the attackers.

Chainalysis attributes the operation to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group. The analytics firm said its strongest evidence came from observing the stolen Binance funds mixing in real time with assets from last month’s Bitget exploit, which had also been attributed to North Korean actors.

The hackers rushed to convert stolen stablecoins, which issuers can freeze, into cryptocurrencies like ETH, which cannot be frozen.

They moved $500 million into a conversion wallet, swapping $325 million for $285 million in ETH within 20 minutes and transferring the remaining $175 million to stopover wallets.

Stablecoin freezes began at 5:14 p.m. ET, as investigators, law enforcement agencies, stablecoin issuers and other industry participants coordinated efforts across multiple blockchains to restrict the movement of stolen funds. Approximately $2.8 billion had been frozen so far.

#5266. NEAR Enters Bitwise Large-Cap Indexes in October Rebalance

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Bitwise’s October 30 rebalance brings NEAR into several indexes, replacing UNI or AVAX depending on the benchmark. Index membership alone does not establish a guaranteed price effect.

Bitwise’s latest scheduled index changes place NEAR in several large-cap benchmarks, with the outgoing constituent depending on the particular index. The changes were announced on October 22 for the October 30 rebalance.

The development is relevant to investors tracking rules-based crypto exposure. It also illustrates why an index announcement needs to be read at the level of the named benchmark, rather than reduced to a general claim that a token has been added to every Bitwise product.

The official rebalance notice says NEAR replaces UNI in the Bitwise 10 Large Cap Crypto Index and the corresponding ex-Bitcoin index. In the Bitwise 10 Select Large Cap Crypto Index, NEAR replaces AVAX.

The notice also lists LIT replacing ETHFI in the decentralized-finance index. No rebalance was scheduled for the BTC/ETH Equal Weight index in that cycle.

Those are constituent decisions. They do not, by themselves, disclose the execution price of any fund trade, the value of assets tracking each index or a completed purchase by every product that uses Bitwise branding.

An index defines a set of assets and a method for weighting and updating them. A fund or other investment product may seek to track that framework, but the benchmark and the vehicle are separate things.

The SEC’s explanation of index funds describes how a tracking product can use different implementation methods and incur costs. The return experienced by an investor can therefore differ from the published index return.

That distinction matters when interpreting additions and removals. A benchmark change establishes how the reference portfolio is defined; it does not reveal every operational decision made by a manager following it.

An addition can create demand from products required to hold the new constituent. The size and timing of that demand depend on how much money follows the index, the target weight and the way managers execute the change.

Traders may also anticipate a publicly announced rebalance before it takes effect. That makes it difficult to infer a simple price response from the inclusion date alone. Other buyers, sellers and broader market conditions remain relevant.

A removal has the same analytical limitation. It may lead to transactions by tracking products, but it is not automatically a judgment that the token’s technology has failed or that all investment managers have rejected it.

The different outgoing assets show why the exact benchmark matters. A main large-cap index, an ex-Bitcoin index and a select index can use different eligibility rules, universes or implementation constraints. Similar names do not make their portfolios identical.

For someone evaluating exposure, the useful questions include how concentrated the index is, how frequently it changes and which risks its rules leave in place. A basket can reduce dependence on one token while remaining highly exposed to the wider crypto market.

The change also creates a clear reference point for future tracking. Published constituent lists and weights can show whether a product is following the intended benchmark, while fees and trading costs explain part of the gap between an index and an investor’s return.

NEAR’s inclusion is a concrete adjustment to Bitwise’s reference portfolios. Claims about inevitable inflows or a guaranteed rally would require evidence beyond the notice. The immediate fact is the new composition, with its market effect dependent on the capital and execution connected to it.

#5263. Italy’s proposed exit tax has an €800K threshold – Who could qualify?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Italy has proposed a 2027 budget bill that would extend an exit-tax regime to certain individuals leaving the country. This will include unrealized crypto gains on crypto assets. This tax could be applied to residents who have lived in Italy at least six out of the last ten years.

The proposal would be effective from the 1st of January 2027. This is if they possess covered assets valued at €800,000 or greater. The exit tax is an unusual application of capital gains tax.

It will be possible for authorities to impose a tax based upon the value of your investment prior to your departure.

Authorities will use the purchase cost of your asset and the current market value of your asset to determine how much of an unrealized gain exists.

Depending on the nature of individual holdings, they might have to liquidate some portion of those holdings or seek outside funding. However, these are mere possibilities since the proposals are still pending approval by parliament.

Moreover, the country’s proposal could significantly impact which jurisdictions that cryptocurrency investors will wish to reside within. As previously stated, the UAE has no personal capital gains tax.

Meanwhile, Portugal has no capital gains tax for gains made during the first 365 days of ownership. Switzerland does not subject most private investors‘ gains from cryptocurrencies to income tax. Still, it does subject such gains to wealth tax.

Also, German law provides exemptions from capital gains tax on certain holdings after one year. Given these differences, relocation choices are likely to become significantly influenced by the presence or absence of tax treatment and the risk of double taxation.

Even so, choosing another jurisdiction may not resolve all ambiguity surrounding exit taxes. In fact, the Italian proposed valuation method utilizes the prices of assets prior to departing a country.

In turn, this places foreign-resident investors at risk due to volatile fluctuations in local markets.

Italy’s proposal could ultimately be extended to include other countries. This is because many existing governments currently tax unrealized gains when investors relocate. Austria levies a 27.5% exit tax on digital currencies.

Moreover, illiquid tokens or locked-up funds can present additional challenges to investors attempting to comply with the requirements. Furthermore, subsequent price drops in an investor’s portfolio may cause investors to pay taxes on gains that were never actually obtained.

All in all, upon becoming law, Italy’s regulation will almost certainly generate debate regarding whether relocation should lead to taxing investors on profits they have never realized.

Crypto holders could face Italy’s proposed exit tax on unrealized gains when relocating abroad.

Italy’s proposal could shape global crypto tax rules on unrealized gains and investor relocation.

#5262. Sui Puts Enforced Spending Limits at the Center of Its AI-Agent Design

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: A Sui design note argues that agents need permissions enforced by the systems they use. Onchain transactions can support those controls, but cannot establish that an agent’s objective is correct.

A useful financial agent needs enough authority to complete a task without repeatedly asking for approval. It also needs boundaries that remain effective if it misunderstands an instruction or encounters misleading information.

An October 28 Sui Foundation design note addresses that tension by focusing on enforceable permissions and records that participants can verify. The discussion is a framework for building safer workflows, not an announcement that all AI agents on Sui have become reliable.

The Foundation’s note argues that boundaries should be enforced by the systems an agent uses, rather than existing only as instructions the agent is expected to remember. It also emphasizes shared terms and verifiable records when multiple organizations participate.

That distinction is straightforward in a payment example. Telling software to spend less than a limit is one control. Giving it credentials that cannot authorize a payment above that limit is another.

The first depends on the agent interpreting and following the rule. The second can reject an action even when the agent has made a mistake. Effective deployment needs both a sensible objective and a mechanism that constrains execution.

Sui’s programmable transaction documentation describes how multiple commands can be grouped so their state changes apply together. If a command fails, the group does not leave the intended asset changes half-completed, although transaction costs still need to be considered.

For an automated workflow, that can help when several onchain steps depend on each other. A purchase and a subsequent movement of the acquired asset can be evaluated as one composed transaction rather than as unrelated operations.

The benefit has limits. Atomic execution does not establish that the price was sensible, the recipient was appropriate or the external service delivered what it promised. It controls how a set of operations completes, not whether the underlying business judgment was good.

A more complex agent may call another service or delegate part of a task. That creates a question about authority: can the next participant do only what the original user permitted, or does delegation accidentally widen the scope?

A robust design would make the answer visible. Permissions could specify a budget, an approved purpose, an expiry and a limited set of counterparties. The system would then check those conditions at the point where an action is authorized.

This is an analytical design principle, not a claim that one blockchain automatically supplies every required control. Developers still need to implement the rules correctly and account for actions that occur outside the chain.

When several businesses interact through software agents, a shared record can help establish which action was authorized and which transaction occurred. That is useful for reconciliation and investigation, particularly when each participant keeps its own internal systems.

The record still needs context. A successful transaction does not prove that a customer received a physical good, that an invoice was genuine or that an offchain input was accurate. Those facts require their own evidence and dispute process.

The strongest implication of Sui’s design note is therefore practical: start with a narrowly defined authority, enforce it at the system boundary and make completed actions inspectable. Expand the scope only when the controls and operational evidence justify doing so.

Blockchain infrastructure can contribute transaction rules and records to that design. The quality of the resulting agent depends on the complete application, including its permissions, information sources and response when something falls outside the expected workflow.

#5261. Ripple’s Bank Approval Leaves XRP On The Sidelines?

Home » Trendsetter News » Ripple’s Bank Approval Leaves XRP On The Sidelines?

Ripple’s bank approval advances its custody and stablecoin business, but may not translate into immediate XRP demand.

XRP funds recorded a $3.61 million net outflow on the day Ripple reportedly secured final approval for its national trust bank. That disconnect anchors a video by crypto commentator Dana Love, who argues the charter primarily advances Ripple’s stablecoin business—not immediate demand for XRP.

Love puts XRP near $1.29 on the reported October 26 approval date and around $1.32 two days later. Over the preceding 30 days, the token had fallen 14.74%, despite a flurry of Ripple announcements around its Swell conference.

The distinction starts with what the bank would actually do. Citing an Office of the Comptroller of the Currency approval letter, Love says Ripple National Trust Bank would provide institutional cryptocurrency custody and manage reserves backing RLUSD, Ripple’s dollar stablecoin.

It would not issue RLUSD itself, accept conventional deposits or make loans. Love describes it as “a vault with a federal badge on the door”—regulated infrastructure, rather than a mechanism that automatically creates token demand.

He also argues that much of the approval was already anticipated. According to the YouTube video research, the OCC conditionally approved Ripple’s application on December 12, 2025, alongside four others; final authorization marked completion of the remaining requirements.

A more direct development for XRP holders, Love says, was BNY’s expanded custody support. He cites a Ripple announcement naming both XRP and RLUSD on BNY’s digital-asset custody platform, potentially removing an operational hurdle for institutions considering the token.

The video cites approximately $1.81 billion in cumulative net inflows into spot XRP ETFs, but just $4.3 million during October 19–23. The reported charter-day withdrawal was followed by a session with no net flows.

Love also questions headlines describing large-wallet concentration as investor accumulation. Two wallets he examined, labeled Ripple 10 and Ripple 11, each received 500 million XRP from escrow. Those balances, he argues, should not be confused with fresh purchases by independent investors.

His outlook remains explicitly speculative: he assigns an 85% probability that an outside institution publicly names Ripple’s bank as its RLUSD custodian by June 30, 2027, versus 20% for XRP custody.

For investors, the distinction is practical: Ripple can expand its regulated business without producing equivalent buying pressure for XRP. Named custody clients and sustained fund inflows would offer stronger evidence of token demand than the charter alone.

In an X post that included a scam alert, Chen stated that there is no compensation for the withdrawal suspension, urging users to stay safe and follow only official Binance accounts' updates.

This comes as scammers circulate fake compensation rewards, in some cases $150. X user @williamclay responded to Chen's post, saying the "free $150 compensation" screenshots circulating are fake, adding that there is no compensation for the withdrawal pause and that users should treat any "check your reward hub" or claim link as a scam.

Binance began restoring customer withdrawals on Sunday, November 1, 2026 after hackers attempted to drain over $6 billion in the biggest cyber theft ever recorded.

In the latest update, withdrawals have now been re-enabled for the following networks and assets: ZEC network: ZEC; TON network: USDT, GRAM; SUI network: SUI; BTC network: BTC;  ETH network: ETH, USDT, USDC;  BSC network: BNB, USDT, USDC;  XRP network: XRP;  Base network: ETH, USDC; DOGE network: DOGE; OP (Optimism) network: ETH, USDT, USDC; Arbitrum network: ARB, ETH, USDT, USDC;  TRX network: TRX, USDT;  SOL: SOL, USDT, USDC;  MATIC (Polygon) network: POL, USDT, USDC;  AVAXC network: AVAX, USDT, USDC.

Withdrawals were temporarily suspended as a precaution while Binance worked to contain the incident's losses, assess its impact, restore affected services, and complete security checks.

#5259. CEXs are losing market share to DEXs – Even when both are shrinking

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Decentralized exchanges (DEXs) are handling 23% of the Spot trading volume done by combined centralized exchanges (CEXs), including Binance, Coinbase, and others.

This marks a record level, and the market share of DEXs has increased by 1100% in the past five years, with an analyst terming it an “impressive” win for DeFi.

What’s impressive is that the market share of DEXs has increased by over 1100% in the past 5 years. DeFi is winning, and the bull case for it has never been more obvious.

Worth noting that the DEX market share doubled between 2024 and 2025. But it later remained flat during the bear market in early 2026. Now, analysts believe that the Binance hack may further favor DEXs, but it’s not all black and white.

In fact, analyst Mago found an interesting pattern in the rising market share. DEX volume has dropped 55% year-on-year (YoY) from $588B in 2025  to $262B in 2026, yet they increased their market share from 17.5% to 23.2%.

So DEXs didn’t take share by growing. They took it by shrinking slower than CEXs. When the market cools, CEX flow leaves. On-chain flow sticks.

In terms of monthly spot volumes, Uniswap and PancakeSwap dominated with 36% of all DEX volumes. Aerodrome and PumpSwap came in third and fourth, respectively.

The largest surge in 2026 happened in July, as the DEX market share increased from 18% to over 22%. This was during the broader market rebound, as Bitcoin recovered from below $57.8K to over $60K and extended its recovery to over $87K in August and September.

In fact, to Andy Cavanaugh, founder of The Rollup, the $6.3B Binance hack, after Bitget’s $388M exploit in September, will further boost this trend.

Major vibe shift over the last 48 hours…Onchain >>> offchain.

And some data points support his outlook. For example, Hyperliquid’s share of aggregate CEX volume increased from 8.0% to 8.3% during the Binance hack. On an individual basis, Hyperliquid was doing an equivalent of 14.5% of Binance’s volume, from a 13.5% low in mid-October.

However, most of these DEXs may not fully repay users in case of hacks like Binance or Bitget did. And with rising AI-enabled security risks across self-custody and other segments, this may also dictate sticky flows or returning traders to CEXs.

Besides, this week, Blockaid flagged an attack targeting the front ends of 12 DeFi projects that were this week, underscoring that hacks are not isolated to centralized exchanges alone. It will be interesting to see if security risks will really drive DEX market share in the future.

#5258. BTCPay Server Tells Merchants to Shut Down After Attackers Sweep Hot Wallets: Are Payments Still Safe?

Bitcoin news: BTCPay Server told merchants to go offline after attackers swept hot wallets on 2.4.1 or older. Here is who is exposed.

In today’s Bitcoin news, BTCPay Server, the free open-source payment processor many Bitcoin merchants run themselves, told every operator to shut down their instance after reports that attackers were sweeping the hot wallets on merchant servers. Less than six hours later, the culprit was old software.

At 04:07 UTC on Monday, the project said its investigation had found an attack vector aimed at servers running version 2.4.1, released on July 23, or older. It has “no credible reports” of drains on the current 2.4.7. BTCPay has not said how much was stolen or how many stores were hit.

That makes this a different kind of Bitcoin news from last week’s Binance hack. No exchange was breached. Merchants who run their own payment stack, the people self-custody is meant to protect, were the target.

So who was exposed, and what should store owners do now?

Unauthorized attackers are reportedly draining hot wallets on @BtcpayServer instances.

Users running BTCPay Server instances are advised to shut them down immediately. pic.twitter.com/H7mXfJLLcD

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 2, 2026

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

An attacker logged in as admin on older servers and emptied the hot wallets. BTCPay Server raised the alarm at 22:25 UTC on Sunday and asked operators to run its shutdown script “until we complete the investigation.”

Two hours later, founder Nicolas Dorier said the project’s own public servers on 2.4.7 were not attacked. “The attacker managed to log in as admin on those instance, we are still trying to figure out how,” he wrote.

📢 Our incident response investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running versions 2.4.1 (Jul 23, 2026) or older.

We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release. We again urge everyone to keep their BTCPay Server… pic.twitter.com/gYxK4Bb7fc

— BTCPay Server (@BtcpayServer) November 2, 2026

A hot wallet keeps its signing keys on the server itself, so it can pay out refunds and payouts automatically. Anyone with admin rights on that server can send the coins too.

Hosting providers moved fast. BTCPay thanked LunaNode and others for shutting down older hosted instances on their own, so some merchants may find their store offline on Monday.

The version history is the story. 2.4.1 shipped on July 23. Two weeks later, 2.4.2 fixed a critical flaw the team said was “being actively exploited,” and five more releases followed, ending with Thursday’s 2.4.7, which fixed 85 findings from an AI security scan Anthropic ran for the project.

Whether this is the same hole as August’s is still open. Dorier said a blog post with more detail is coming.

Only if it still runs 2.4.1 or older, on what the project knows so far. “For those who already updated at least once since the release of 2.4.2, there is no reason to panic,” Dorier wrote at 04:10 UTC.

The reported drains all hit hot wallets. Stores that receive into a watch-only wallet keep their signing keys off the server altogether.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

No. BTC sat at $77,890 when the alert went out and traded at $78,102 on Binance at 07:40 UTC on Monday, up 0.3% in a day. The market is still chewing on last week’s Binance hack.

That hack set the floor. Bitcoin fell to $76,326 on October 30, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average), now at $76,512, and buyers have held above it for three days. Above, the 50-day EMA at $80,293 is now overhead, and $81,971, the October 29 high before the hack, caps the range.

The Fear & Greed Index reads 37, fear, and BTC is down 2.5% on the week.

The report examined 20 exchanges, including 11 selected for in-depth analysis based on market share, trading volume, and open interest.

In Q3, MEXC recorded $1.069 trillion in total trading volume, ranking fourth among the exchanges covered in the report. Its market share reached 8.91%, up 0.38 percentage points from the previous quarter, marking the third-largest increase among major exchanges. Derivatives trading volume reached $963 billion, representing a 9.67% market share and ranking fourth among exchanges. MEXC recorded $86 billion in commodity perpetuals trading volume in Q3, accounting for 17.43% of the market and ranking second among exchanges. MEXC recorded $117 billion in equity perpetuals trading volume in Q3, representing a 7.28% market share and ranking fourth among the nine exchanges tracked. Its trading volume was just $5 billion behind the third-ranked exchange.

#5255. Why Coinbase Bitcoin Discount Just Hit a Yearly High

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Classic crypto market metrics have suddenly stopped reflecting reality. Bitcoin’s discount on the U.S. exchange Coinbase relative to the international Binance has hit a yearly high, with the Coinbase Premium Index collapsing to around −0.06%.

In normal times, such a chart gives traders a cold sweat: the index going deep into the red zone means that large funds in the U.S. have started massively dumping crypto.

However, the current collapse of the indicator turned out to be a technical illusion. It was provoked by the emergency freeze of operations on Binance immediately after a large-scale hack of the exchange, which completely blocked classic cross-exchange arbitrage.

The anomalous price gap coincided with the largest incident in the industry’s history: on October 29–30, hackers attacked Binance’s hot wallets, withdrawing about $6.3 billion. The exchange promptly froze half of the stolen funds on the blockchain, and the head of the platform promised to fully cover the remaining client losses from the SAFU reserve fund.

Nevertheless, amid the panic, the price of Bitcoin dropped to $77,000–$78,000.

To localize the problem, Binance completely shut the gateways — it temporarily banned any deposits and withdrawals of funds. This decision instantly paralyzed cross-exchange arbitrage. Large players physically could not buy the temporarily cheaper Bitcoin on Coinbase and transfer it to Binance to even out the price.

Liquidity was locked inside the platforms, which caused the discount to artificially swell to its widest level in a year.

As noted by Galaxy Research’s head of research Alex Thorn, due to the blocking of transactions, the discount on Coinbase temporarily stopped being a signal of weak demand in the U.S.

On November 1, Binance announced a phased reopening of withdrawals, starting with BTC and ETH. Now the market is waiting to see how quickly arbitrageurs eliminate the gap. If the gap closes in the coming days, it means the anomaly was purely technical.

If the negative spread becomes entrenched, it will be an alarming signal of a real cooling of American capital.

#5251. Nvidia, Nike and 48 Other Companies Oppose OKX Stock Tokenization Plan

A total of 50 companies, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Nike (NKE), have officially raised objections to the trading of tokenized shares on a new platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

As per the most recent public notice by the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), OKXICE, the total number of companies objecting to the initiative has reached 50 as of Oct. 30.

The total increased from 38 companies on Oct. 28, with 12 additional companies raising objections in just two days.

The new names that recently raised objections include Nvidia, Nike, Costco (COST), Micron Technology (MU) and Reddit (RDDT).

Other companies that have recently raised objections include cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike (CRWD), Corning (GLW), Bloom Energy (BE), IREN (IREN), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Big names in the financial world, including JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Wells Fargo (WFC), have also raised objections.

Some other prominent names include Walmart (WMT), Coca-Cola (KO), McDonald's (MCD), Eli Lilly (LLY), Adobe (ADBE) and Dell Technologies (DELL).

OKXICE is a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Each of them owns a 50% stake in the joint venture.

The goal is to enable tokenized versions of traditional US stocks to be traded on the blockchain.

Instead of buying these shares on a traditional brokerage platform, eligible investors can trade blockchain tokens that represent ownership interests in the underlying securities.

The platform will be open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, as per the company's public notice.

The planned platform will be based on a temporary regulatory exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Sept. 17.

However, the regulator gave companies the option to object to any unauthorized third-party tokenization of their shares.

If a company submits an objection within the specified timeframe, then its third-party tokenized shares cannot be offered by the platform under the exemption.

#5249. Bitcoin White Paper Turns 18 With Payment Verification Still at Its Core

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Satoshi Nakamoto introduced the Bitcoin paper on October 31, 2008. Eighteen years later, its central contribution remains a way to verify payment history without a central transaction ledger.

Bitcoin’s white paper reached its eighteenth anniversary on October 31. The original mailing-list message survives as a compact announcement of a peer-to-peer electronic cash proposal, rather than a forecast of market capitalization or institutional demand.

Revisiting that document offers a useful way to separate Bitcoin’s foundational payment mechanism from the many financial products and businesses now associated with the asset.

Satoshi Nakamoto’s October 31, 2008 message introduced a system intended to prevent double-spending through a peer-to-peer network. The paper itself combines digital signatures with a shared proof-of-work history.

A signature can show that a key authorized a transfer. It cannot, by itself, establish that the same funds were not also offered in a competing transaction. The network’s history provides the additional ordering needed to decide which valid spend is recognized.

That is the central distinction behind the proposal. It is about reaching and verifying an agreed transaction history, with security assumptions that the paper makes explicit.

A payment broadcast to the network and a payment included in a block are different states. Additional blocks build on the accepted history, changing the effort needed to replace it with a competing one.

Bitcoin’s developer guide on payment processing discusses how merchants can monitor payments and account for confirmation risk. A business needs a policy suited to the value and circumstances of the transaction, rather than treating every incoming notification as equally final.

The commercial implication is that payment acceptance involves a judgment about risk. A low-value purchase and a large irreversible delivery may justify different procedures even when they use the same underlying network.

Bitcoin can provide evidence about a transfer of coins. It does not independently establish that a seller shipped the right product, that a buyer understood the agreement or that a recipient address belongs to the intended person.

Those questions sit around the payment mechanism. They can be addressed through contracts, identity checks, escrow arrangements or other business processes, but they are not solved merely by placing a transaction onchain.

This helps explain why direct settlement and customer protection are distinct design problems. A system can make a payment difficult to reverse while still needing a practical method for resolving mistakes or disputes about the transaction’s purpose.

The white paper is historically important, but it is not a complete description of every feature in modern Bitcoin software. The network has accumulated implementation work, standards and operational practice since the proposal was introduced.

Nor does the document establish what Bitcoin should be worth at any particular time. Market demand, access, competing assets and individual financial circumstances are separate from the technical mechanism described in its pages.

That separation makes the anniversary more informative. The enduring question is how participants can check a payment history without relying on one institution to keep the authoritative ledger, and what assumptions make that verification meaningful.

Eighteen years after the announcement, the paper remains useful because it states the problem and the proposed solution with unusual focus. Reading it alongside current documentation makes it easier to judge claims about Bitcoin on their own terms: which part is cryptographic verification, which part is a service built around it and which part is an expectation about future demand.

#5248. Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 in 2026, More Than Triple 2025, Yet Without Binance the Year Ran Quieter: How Did Bitcoin and Ethereum React After Major Hacks?

Crypto hack losses hit $8.74B in 2026 vs $2.51B in 2025. Here’s how Bitcoin and Ether moved a day, a week and a month after major hacks.

Crypto hack losses reached $8.74 billion in 2026 by October 31, more than three times the $2.51 billion lost over the same ten months of 2025, after the October 29 Binance breach alone added $6.36 billion.

Take Binance out and the picture flips. The rest of 2026 comes to $2.38 billion, about 5% less than 2025 at the same point, even though attackers hit 325 targets against 120 a year earlier. More attacks, smaller hauls, and then one enormous one.

The market has its own pattern. Across the ten largest hacks since January 2025, Bitcoin’s move on the day of the attack ranged from -4.1% to +1.9%. A month later, for the nine with a full month of data, the range ran from -15.5% to +19.9%, and it followed whatever the broader market was doing.

The 2025 hacks landed in falling markets, and every one was followed by a lower Bitcoin price a month later. Most of 2026’s landed in rising ones.

So how bad has 2026 really been, and what does history say about the weeks after Binance?

The size of the biggest theft. Through September, 2026 was running behind 2025: $2.24 billion lost against $2.48 billion. Then Binance lost $6.36 billion across ten blockchains in one night, more than all of 2025’s hacks put together.

The two years share a culprit. The FBI tied 2025’s largest crypto hack, the $1.4 billion Bybit theft on February 21, to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Chainalysis now ties Binance to the same unit. The biggest hacks of each year:

The rest of 2026 looks different from 2025 too. There were 325 incidents through October, almost three times 2025’s 120, and five 2026 hacks topped $290 million, against one in 2025. Stolen keys and cross-chain bridges did most of the damage outside Binance.

The gross number also overstates what stays lost. CertiK’s October tally counts $3.03 billion frozen or returned, mostly Binance funds caught on-chain, which cuts the month’s adjusted losses to about $3.47 billion. Trackers also disagree on the year: CertiK puts 2026 at $9.2 billion gross and 2025 at $3.35 billion, while DefiLlama has $8.74 billion and $2.72 billion.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

A small dip on the day, then the market’s own trend. The heatmap compares Bitcoin and Ether with their close the day before each of the ten biggest hacks since 2025.

Bybit is the closest match to Binance: a North Korean exchange theft over $1 billion. Bitcoin lost 14.2% within a week of it, with US tariff fears weighing on markets that week too, and it was still 12.4% lower a month on.

Binance is following a gentler path so far. From the October 28 close to Monday:

Neither yet. Bitcoin trades at $77,870 on Binance, flat on the day, and has held above its October 30 low of $76,326 for three days, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average) at $76,512.

After Bybit, Bitcoin lost its floor within a week. After most of 2026’s hacks, it was higher a month later. The line between the two is clear on the chart: the 200-day EMA below, and the 50-day EMA at $80,293 above.

The crypto hack record says the first day rarely decides much. What Bitcoin does at the 200-day EMA over the next few weeks will show which path this one takes.

Intersect, a Cardano ecosystem governance entity, has recommended that stake pool operators (SPOs) upgrade their systems to patch a critical Linux flaw.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, could allow an attacker to inject and execute a remote malicious code remotely. According to Red Hat’s security brief, the flaw has a CVSS severity score of 9.8 and system-wide scope across major Linux systems, including Ubuntu, which powers Cardano.

The flaw is within the Linux kernel subsystem that handles internet connections ( IPv4 TCP connections). It can allow an attacker to exploit a node (block producer) or relay, effectively leading to node crashes or data corruption.

So far, some Linux systems have been fixed with relevant patches. Fixes for Ubuntu are currently being expedited, and Intersect wants SPOs to upgrade swiftly when the patched releases are out.

If you run a stake pool, check which kernel your block producer and relays use, and apply the fixed kernel and reboot as soon as your distribution publishes it.

Intersect oversees the Cardano codebase and treasury operations. Other top entities like the Cardano Foundation and EMURGO handle the nonprofit and commercial arms, respectively.

The SPOs are equivalent to validators on Solana or Ethereum, as they process block transactions. Each SPO runs the Cardano node’s system and is recommended to update their system accordingly.

The bug was initially flagged by Anthropic and affected several systems globally, underscoring the security risks and benefits of AI models.

That said, ADA’s sentiment has dropped to August fear lows. The August fear turned out to be a great buy signal as ADA rallied 62% from $0.17 to $0.28. It’s unclear whether the current fear signal will also be a buying opportunity.

However, it appeared some whales deemed it a great buying opportunity as well. According to CryptoQuant’s data, whale activity has spiked near the $0.19 price zone.

A similar pattern was seen when ADA price dipped to this area in mid-September and stopped the pullback.

If the whale activity and near-term pattern repeat, buyers may defend the $0.19. In fact, the level has acted as support since late August. The immediate bullish target would be $0.22 if a rebound happens at this level, presenting a 15% upside potential.

But if Bitcoin records more losses, ADA sellers may attempt to crack the $0.19 support.

#5244. Noble USDC Holders Face New Migration Phase as CCTP Limits Start Winding Down

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Circle’s published schedule begins reducing legacy CCTP burn limits from October 31. Noble has a separate January 2027 pause, so holders and integrators need to distinguish the deadlines.

The wind-down of Circle’s legacy cross-chain infrastructure has entered a new scheduled phase, with burn-limit reductions due to begin on October 31. For USDC holders on Noble, that sits inside a longer transition that ends with a planned contract and route pause in January.

The dates matter because a token can remain transferable on its existing chain while one of the routes used to move it elsewhere becomes more restricted.

Circle’s CCTP V1 deprecation notice says burn limits begin reducing on October 31, ahead of a general legacy-contract pause on December 1. It states that V2 uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible with V1.

Its Noble-specific notice sets January 12, 2027 as the pause date for Noble’s USDC contract and remaining CCTP routes. Noble will not receive V2 support. New Noble minting was scheduled to stop on October 13.

These are the issuer’s published schedules. They should not be replaced with an assumption that every route reached a zero limit immediately on October 31. Circle also warns that, after December 1, Noble exits may be limited to destinations still supporting V1. January 12 therefore does not guarantee every route remains open until that date.

When a protocol version uses different contracts and APIs, an application has to change the systems it calls and the assumptions it makes about responses. Updating a logo or displaying a new route name is not sufficient.

Integrators also need to account for transfers already in progress. A source-chain action, an attestation and a destination-chain completion are related steps, and the status of one does not establish that the whole process has finished.

The operational objective is to avoid a gap in which users can begin a transfer that the application no longer knows how to complete. Clear route availability and handling of pending transfers are therefore part of the migration work.

USDC issued on one blockchain is not interchangeable at the interface level with every asset bearing the same ticker elsewhere. A receiving service has to support the actual network and token form being sent.

That distinction becomes more important during a sunset. A venue might support a destination chain while no longer accepting deposits from an older route, or it might require a conversion step with its own terms and liquidity.

The Cosmos community-pool migration proposal illustrates the issue at treasury level, describing a planned move from Noble-issued to Injective-issued USDC. A proposal records an intended process; its publication alone does not prove the migration has completed.

Circle says remaining Noble balances will be snapshotted on the January pause date, with a manual redemption process beginning the following day and subject to eligibility and compliance requirements. That is a fallback process, not the same experience as an ordinary automated transfer.

For holders and services, the useful preparation is to establish which supported route applies, what conditions govern it and how completion will be verified. An asset arriving at an unintended address or through an unsupported network can create problems that a ticker symbol does not reveal.

The broader lesson is that blockchain availability and issuer support have separate lifecycles. A network can continue operating while a particular stablecoin issuer retires contracts or infrastructure on it.

The current development is the start of the scheduled reduction phase. The next checks should focus on current route status and verified completion, while keeping the December legacy deadline and Noble’s January deadline clearly distinct.

#5243. 40 Million XRP Moved From Binance Hacker Wallet

Blockchain tracking service Whale Alert has reported that a wallet linked to the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack has just sent 40 million XRP (~$50.5 million) to a mystery address.

On Nov. 2, Whale Alert shared information about the huge XRP transfer, noting that the transaction initiator is an address tagged "Binance Hack 2026."

The huge transfer took place at 03:56 UTC, Whale Alert data shows. The transaction involved 40 million XRP (~$50.46 million).

Interestingly, just 50 seconds before that, Whale Alert reported another transfer of 40 million XRP.

Another 40 million XRP (~$50.44 million) was also sent from the wallet tagged as "Binance Hack 2026" to a mystery address.

In total, these two transfers involved 80 million XRP (~$100.9 million).

Both transfers originated from the same wallet but were sent to separate mystery addresses.

It is still unclear why these transfers were made. There is no sign that these funds have been sent to a crypto exchange or sold yet.

The transactions took place just days after Binance faced one of the biggest cryptocurrency hacks ever.

The massive XRP transfers came shortly after Binance started to restore cryptocurrency withdrawals following the unprecedented security breach the cryptocurrency exchange faced.

On Nov. 1, Binance annonced that the exchange would restore withdrawals in phases for 15 blockchain networks, including XRP Ledger, Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Solana.

It also mentioned that withdrawals would be gradually restored for other networks, such as Tron, Dogecoin, Zcash, Avalanche, Sui, Polygon and Arbitrum.

The first stage of withdrawal resumption was set to take place between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC on Nov. 1.

After Binance faced a security breach on Oct. 29, which led to the loss of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from its hot wallets, it temporarily paused withdrawals.

The exchange noted that withdrawals would be restored gradually after the security and infrastructure checks had been performed.

Binance also said that XRP balances were already fully backed, as were those of other major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and BNB.

Binance claimed that, as of Nov. 1, around 95% of affected assets had been replenished. The remaining 5% consists primarily of less liquid cryptocurrencies.

#5241. Kraken Prop Adds Commodity Signals With Lower Non-Crypto Commissions

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Kraken Prop has added six commodity markets and reduced non-crypto commissions on most plans. Participants submit simulated trade signals; they do not own the underlying commodity positions.

Kraken Prop has expanded its offering to include gold, silver, oil and other commodity markets, while reducing the commission applied to non-crypto activity on most plans. The October 29 announcement places the expansion within the company’s evaluation and performance-based payout service.

The product’s structure deserves to be stated clearly at the outset. Kraken says participants provide trade signals and do not hold real positions; the stated trading limits are simulated.

Kraken’s announcement lists gold, silver, WTI oil, Brent oil, copper and natural gas. On plans other than Lite, the non-crypto commission falls from four basis points to two basis points per side. Crypto-market commissions are unchanged.

The company says the commodity offering is available where Kraken Prop operates, excluding the UAE. Plan-specific leverage and notional caps differ, so a maximum quoted for one tier should not be applied to every participant.

The announcement also identifies the service as unregulated and says evaluation fees become non-refundable once trading begins. Those terms are material to understanding what a customer is purchasing.

Two basis points equals 0.02%. Applied to a hypothetical $50,000 notional signal, that is $10 on entry and another $10 on exit, assuming the notional remains the same. At four basis points per side, the corresponding total would be $40 rather than $20.

That calculation illustrates the fee change, not an expected profit. A strategy still has to account for price movement, spreads, the platform’s evaluation rules and other applicable costs.

Lower transaction costs can make a difference to a frequently traded strategy, but they cannot turn an unfavorable price outcome into a sound trade by themselves. The proportionate benefit also depends on how often and at what size the participant trades.

Kraken’s product page describes the commodity offering within its Prop service. A participant is not buying a bar of gold, taking delivery of oil or acquiring a conventional futures position simply because the interface displays those markets.

The relevant claim is instead against the program under its terms, including the conditions for evaluation, drawdown limits and any payout. That distinction changes what should be compared with other financial products.

A large simulated account number is also not a cash balance the participant can withdraw. It represents the environment in which performance is assessed. The amount available for payout, if any, follows the program’s rules rather than the headline account size.

A service can keep quoting a reference market when conventional venues are closed. The quality and responsiveness of those quotations then depend on its pricing methodology and available information, rather than on an assumption that every underlying market is equally liquid at every hour.

This is particularly relevant to commodity news arriving outside normal trading sessions. A visible price is not, on its own, evidence of deep executable liquidity in the underlying physical or futures market.

For someone assessing the offering, the meaningful questions concern the exact contract, the calculation of performance, the treatment of unusual market conditions and the path from a successful evaluation to an actual payment.

The expansion broadens the range of signals Kraken Prop participants can submit and changes a specific part of the cost structure. It should be understood on those terms, without confusing simulated trading capacity with ownership of commodities or a guarantee of income.

#5240. Hackers Use Claude, Gemini and Kimi to Identify Valuable Crypto Targets

Cybercriminals are using popular artificial intelligence (AI) models like Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini and Moonshot AI's Kimi AI to evaluate the financial worth of potential victims, including those owning cryptocurrencies.

Cybersecurity researchers at Cisco Talos detailed in a new report how a new type of Windows malware dubbed VOLTA-AUTODOXER, or simply VOLTA, steals sensitive data and uses AI tools to identify potentially lucrative targets among compromised users.

Compared to traditional information-stealing malware, which mainly steals passwords and credentials, VOLTA can also analyze stolen data to build victim profiles and determine what assets hackers can potentially exploit for profit.

Notably, one of VOLTA's most dangerous features is its ability to extract sensitive crypto wallet information, including recovery seed phrases, which can potentially give attackers access to digital assets.

VOLTA also includes features that can crack cryptocurrency wallet vaults, posing a big risk for people who store their crypto wallet credentials on their computers.

But its features are not just limited to stealing crypto.

As explained by Cisco Talos security researcher Ryan Fetterman, VOLTA can also grab saved browser passwords, payment card info, authentication tokens, email credentials and active sessions on popular platforms like Telegram, Discord, Steam and Roblox.

It can also extract info from Outlook accounts and Slack workspaces, as well as other personal and professional information on the infected system.

The malware also takes things further by analyzing victims' email accounts to grab more personal data.

For example, it can scan Gmail accounts for purchase confirmations and receipts from services like Amazon, PayPal, Walmart, DoorDash and Uber Eats.

This way, attackers can get more details about a victim's identity, home address, job and spending habits.

The malware can send stolen data to AI models via the OpenRouter service, which provides access to several AI models.

It first tries to process the collected data using Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6.

If the model fails to process the request, VOLTA is hardcoded to try Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 and Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash.

As explained by Cisco Talos, VOLTA specifically looks for refusal responses before attempting to use a different AI model.

It feeds the collected data to the AI models and asks them to analyze it, providing a comprehensive evaluation of a victim's financial worth.

It can also help identify valuable assets and then rank them based on how lucrative they may be. It can also score a victim's cybersecurity.

Essentially, it allows hackers to use AI models to find potentially lucrative targets without the need to manually sift through stolen data.

#5239. Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Home » Cardano (ADA) » Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Cardano Foundation just opened the path for multi-billion tokenized shares on the mainstream Layer-1 network.

The Cardano Foundation has joined Switzerland’s Capital Markets and Technology Association, and the group has recognized Cardano’s CIP-0113 programmable token standard as equivalent to its own CMTAT framework for certifying tokenized shares.

The move advances regulated securities tokenization on the network at the same time ADA trades in a clear bearish structure and tests the $0.182 area.

The Foundation announced membership in CMTA on October 29. CMTA is the Swiss industry association that develops practical standards for issuing and managing securities on distributed ledgers.

Following the mainnet launch of CIP-0113 earlier in the month, CMTA’s Expert Committee treated a reviewed Cardano implementation of the standard as technically equivalent to CMTAT for equity securities.

NEW: Cardano Foundation joins CMTA, the Swiss entity "setting the standard for tokenized capital markets," alongside members including UBS, with $7T in AUM. CMTA has recognized $ADA's CIP-113 as "equivalent to the CMTAT—meaning issuers can use it to tokenize certifiable shares." pic.twitter.com/iqmz811b4U

Issuers that meet the deployment conditions can therefore use it to tokenize shares that are eligible for CMTA’s certification process.

CIP-0113 went live on Cardano’s (ADA) mainnet on October 7 without a hard fork. It lets issuers attach compliance rules.

KYC and AML checks, sanctions screening, freeze and seize powers, and transfer restrictions, directly to native Cardano tokens. The ledger enforces those rules on every transfer, mint, or burn.

The blokchain recognition is limited to tokenized shares (equity), does not extend to tokenized debt or Cardano’s base-layer infrastructure, and still requires each issuance to satisfy Swiss legal and technical checks.

Shortly after launch, Veridian, a digital-identity company spun out from the Foundation, tokenized its own shares as ledger-based securities under Switzerland’s DLT Act using the standard, becoming the first publicly identified issuer to do so.

While the institutional groundwork advances, ADA’s chart tells a different short-term story. On the 4-hour timeframe the token continues a downtrend of lower highs and lower lows. It has slipped below the $0.20 support zone and is testing the $0.182 area.

Until that reclaim occurs, bears remain in control and further downside remains possible if buyers fail to defend the current zone.

The CMTA membership and CIP-0113 equivalence give Cardano a clearer route into regulated tokenized capital markets in Switzerland, where ledger-based securities already have a defined legal framework. MSB Intel says the opportunities are in the trillions.

The Cardano Foundation has joined CMTA, the Swiss body that sets tokenized securities standards, whose members include UBS, Pictet and Lombard Odier.UBS alone has $7.328T in invested assets.@Cardano pic.twitter.com/Vb4bVAac0X

No doubt, this is the kind of standard work that makes real-world assets (RWAs) practical rather than purely experimental.
