#5237. Hong Kong Advances EnsembleTX to 24/7 Settlement and Plans Stablecoin Trials

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s November 2 update says EnsembleTX now supports 24/7 real-value settlement and reports completed trials of tokenized Exchange Fund Bills. Regulated stablecoins are planned for further trials. These developments put the cash side of tokenization into focus.

A tokenized asset can be transferred on a network that never closes, yet the payment needed to buy it may still depend on a bank service with limited hours. That mismatch leaves a buyer or seller waiting, funding an account in advance or accepting exposure to an intermediary while the other leg catches up.

Extending the money leg can therefore be more consequential than simply adding another token to a trading platform. Consider a treasury team that needs to rebalance after an overseas market opens. If both assets and settlement funds are available, it may complete the adjustment when the need arises rather than hold extra idle cash until its home market resumes.

That is a conditional operational benefit, not a claim that every Hong Kong financial product has become available continuously. Access still depends on participating institutions, eligible instruments and the specific arrangements supporting a transaction.

The bill trials address a different question from whether an issuer can create a digital representation of a security: can that instrument support secondary trading and financing after issuance? A primary sale demonstrates distribution. Repeated transfers and collateral use test the infrastructure that lets an asset function as part of a market.

In a repurchase transaction, one party provides cash against securities with an agreement to reverse the trade. The operational challenge is keeping collateral, payment and the eventual return of both consistent. Automation could reduce manual reconciliation, but only if the records used by the counterparties describe the same obligations.

The relevant performance measures would include settlement failures, time spent resolving exceptions and the amount of cash that participants must keep available. A faster confirmation screen alone cannot establish that a market has become cheaper to operate.

Hong Kong’s official stablecoin register identifies licensed issuers. That licensing framework should be distinguished from the technical ability to move a token. A regulated issuer has defined responsibilities; an integrated settlement system must still decide how to treat its liabilities.

For a participant, the questions include who can redeem, how redemption requests are handled outside normal banking hours, and what happens if an intermediary cannot process a payment. Bringing a stablecoin into a trial gives institutions a setting in which to examine those interactions. It does not make the token identical to central-bank money or a commercial-bank deposit.

The planned expansion could also test whether different forms of money are interchangeable at the moment a transaction needs them. If conversion remains fragmented, continuous asset trading can still leave liquidity trapped in the wrong place.

The most useful follow-up would show what participants actually settle, how often they do it and how the system behaves when a transaction needs intervention. Volumes matter, but so do operational details such as failed instructions and the ability to reconcile a position after an outage.

For crypto markets, the significance is the widening set of institutional workflows that can operate with tokenized instruments. It is an infrastructure development with a concrete settlement objective. Its success will be visible in reliable transfers and usable liquidity, rather than an automatic increase in the value of any public-chain token.

#5234. Utah Files Felony Charges Against Kalshi, Co-Founders Over Sports Bets

Utah Files Felony Charges Against Kalshi, Co-Founders Over Sports Bets

Utah has filed criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and its two co-founders, accusing them of illegally promoting gambling in the state, ABC4 reported on Wednesday.

KalshiEX LLC, CEO Tarek Mansour and COO Luana Lopes Lara face one count of pattern of unlawful activity, a second-degree felony, 12 counts of online gambling promotion, a third-degree felony, and one count of gambling promotion, a misdemeanor, according to the charging documents.

"Gambling is illegal in Utah, whether you place the bet, run the game, or promote it. Calling it a 'prediction market' doesn't change what it is, and being federally registered doesn't put a company above the law," Utah Attorney General Derek Brown said in a statement.

According to the charges, a special agent with the Utah State Bureau of Investigation set up an undercover account as a Utah resident and placed 12 wagers on sports including NFL and college games in September, passing a location check that confirmed he was in the state. Kalshi earned proceeds from the fees it charged on each bet, prosecutors allege.

Brown's office did not say what penalties it would seek, though the felony charges carry the possibility of jail time, the Associated Press reported.

"This is a crazy overreach; Utah is clearly playing politics," Kalshi said in a statement. "We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona."

The charges escalate a dispute that already involves the federal government. Utah, where the state constitution bans gambling, sued Kalshi in state court last week. On Tuesday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Utah to block its enforcement actions against CFTC-registered exchanges, making it the 10th state the agency has taken to court.

"Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets," CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said.

Utah has already won one round. In August, U.S. District Judge Robert Shelby rejected Kalshi's own bid to block enforcement, ruling that federal law "does not preempt Utah's ability to enforce its anti-gambling laws." Kalshi is appealing to the Tenth Circuit, which denied its request for an injunction in September.

President Donald Trump has backed the CFTC, saying in May that it was "critically important that the CFTC's exclusive authority over Prediction Markets is maintained," and calling several state officials who had challenged the platforms "scum."

Federal appeals courts have split on whether states can apply gambling laws to prediction markets. The Third Circuit ruled in April that New Jersey cannot regulate sports contracts on the platforms, while the Sixth and Ninth Circuits sided with Ohio, Tennessee and Nevada in August and September. New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to settle the question, backed by 39 other states and the District of Columbia.

"Different judges in different places say different things," Isaac Rose-Berman, a gambling policy fellow at the American Institute for Boys and Men, told ABC4. "It's just going to keep escalating and eventually get to the Supreme Court."

#5233. Sui’s 40M TPS Demo Comes With an Off-Chain Caveat

Home » Trendsetter News » Sui’s 40M TPS Demo Comes With an Off-Chain Caveat

Sui’s 40M TPS demonstration highlights blockchain’s push for speed, but its off-chain design raises questions about the actual figures.

Sui reached more than 40 million transactions per second in a demonstration highlighted by crypto commentator Linda, but those transactions did not run directly through its mainnet.

The demonstration, which she says took place at Sui Base Camp during Token2049 in early October, used “tunnels” to process activity off-chain before settling results on-chain. That makes it a different proposition from sustained mainnet throughput.

Linda connects the test to Sui chain push into AI-agent infrastructure. A Sui chain co-founder’s clip featured in the video describes plans for agent coordination, payments and auditable activity, alongside collaboration with Google.

The strategic ambition is clear; the demonstration alone does not establish production demand.

She describes potential private versions of Ethereum applications such as Uniswap and Aave, plus private swaps accessible through existing Solana wallets.

She also reports that Midnight has passed one million mainnet transactions and that daily transactions increased nearly 400-fold in a month.

The YouTube video does not supply the starting daily transaction count, limiting what that growth multiple says about sustained adoption.

Linda reports that Solana’s Alpenglow upgrade is live on mainnet beta, citing a reduction in finality from roughly 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds. Those figures imply about an 85-fold improvement, rather than the approximately 40-fold increase stated in the narration.

For Cardano, she describes Leios as approaching rollout through the Dijkstra hard fork, with initial throughput expected at three to five times current levels and later improvements targeting 10–15 times. These remain forward-looking claims in the video, not demonstrated performance results.

#5231. XRP Final Move: Binance Empties Hacked Wallet of Last $101 Million

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

The compromised hot wallet of the Binance exchange has been completely emptied. Blockchain tracker Whale Alert recorded two identical transactions of 40 million XRP each (around $101 million in total), which went to a new address 50 seconds apart.

This is the platform's corporate address rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. After the October 29 attack, the wallet received an official red "Reported as hacked" label in network explorers.

As a result of this final transfer, the address's balance dropped to 23.7 XRP (around $30) — the exchange fully removed the remaining funds, moving them to new internal wallets.

This transfer effectively closes activity on the vulnerable address and is a planned technical consolidation of the remaining balances. The transfer of assets followed a large-scale cross-chain attack on Binance that began on October 29. Total damage across ten different blockchains is estimated at $6.3 billion, making the incident the largest crypto theft in history.

Hot wallets on the XRP Ledger took the first hit: within five minutes at the start of the attack, a total of 233.46 million XRP (around $296 million) was withdrawn from them.

The specifics of the XRPL network itself oblige the exchange to fully zero out hacked addresses. Unlike most stablecoins (such as USDT or USDC), where issuers can forcibly freeze funds, the XRP Ledger code has no protocol-level blocking function.

Neither Ripple nor independent XRP Ledger developers has no technical ability to stop transactions, so leaving any available balance on a hacked wallet is unsafe. Moving the remaining 80 million XRP to new wallets isolated by the platform eliminates the risk of repeated withdrawals.

For the XRP ecosystem, this incident became an absolute all-time negative record, surpassing the September hack of the Bitget exchange, in which 103 million XRP ($157 million) was lost, multiple times over.

At the same time, no panic has been recorded on the market. Binance has fully restored withdrawal operations for clients. The platform's management officially stated that all net user losses will be compensated 1:1 from corporate reserves and SAFU fund money.

The transfer of the last $101 million in XRP likely puts an end to operations with the hacked address, minimizing further technical risks for the platform.

#5230. Animoca Announces ADGM Fund-Management Permission for Institutional Expansion

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Animoca Brands has added a fund-management authorization in Abu Dhabi to its institutional business. The company announced on November 2 that Animoca Asset Management (AD) Limited had received Financial Services Permission from ADGM’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority to manage collective investment funds in or from the financial centre.

The company announcement follows an earlier effective date: the ADGM register dates permission 250097 to October 13, 2026. It prohibits dealing with retail clients and holding or controlling client assets, defining a narrower scope than a general licence to provide every crypto service.

A professionally managed fund can bring several decisions into one structure: the investment mandate, who has discretion over transactions, how assets are valued and what investors receive in return for contributing capital. That can make a digital-asset strategy easier to assess than a collection of direct token purchases.

It also creates a clearer place to ask difficult questions. An investor can examine the manager’s authority, the legal entity responsible for the assets and the process for calculating performance. Those questions remain important whether a portfolio holds tokens, equity in blockchain companies or another form of exposure.

For Animoca, the potential commercial advantage is being able to meet an allocator through a regulated investment-management structure. Permission does not itself supply investor demand, a track record for a new strategy or a pool of committed money.

The group’s presence elsewhere in the UAE offers relevant context without changing the meaning of this approval. Dubai’s VARA public register separately lists Animoca Brands Middle East Advisory FZCO for broker-dealer and management and investment services, with institutional and qualified-investor conditions.

The entities and regulators should not be collapsed into a single blanket licence. A client dealing with an investment manager needs to know which company signs the agreement, what service it provides and which permissions apply to that relationship.

This becomes particularly relevant when a group operates across investments, advisory work, technology and token-related services. A recognizable brand can span several businesses whose responsibilities differ. Documentation needs to follow the actual service, rather than relying on the reputation of the parent.

An investor with a wide network of technology businesses may have access to early projects, founders and commercial information that an outside allocator cannot easily obtain. That can be useful when evaluating young markets where conventional financial histories are limited.

The same proximity creates questions about potential conflicts. A fund might encounter opportunities involving companies in which a related business already has an interest. Investors would reasonably want to understand how such situations are identified, reviewed and disclosed, without assuming from the authorization alone that any particular transaction is planned.

Valuation is another practical issue. A liquid token, a venture investment and a contractual right to future revenue can behave very differently when markets weaken. Combining them in a strategy requires a coherent explanation of liquidity and how often investors can withdraw.

The next meaningful disclosures would concern named funds, their objectives, eligible investors, custody arrangements, fees and redemption terms. Those details turn a broad institutional ambition into something a prospective allocator can compare with other options.

Capital raised is also different from assets already invested. A fund can secure commitments before deploying them, and a product can launch without immediately reaching material scale. Keeping those stages separate makes progress easier to measure.

For now, Animoca has reported an additional regulated capability in a market central to its regional expansion. The authorization strengthens the framework through which the group can pursue institutional business; the quality of the investment products built within that framework will determine the longer-term outcome.

New account creation on the XRP Ledger jumped 142.4%, according to XRPScan data. It points to renewed interest in the ecosystem, even though XRP is still struggling to get its bullish momentum back.

XRPScan counted 7,734 newly activated accounts on November 1, 2026, up 33% from the day before and far above the network's 30-day average of roughly 3,500 new accounts a day.

Wallet creation is clearly speeding up. What's behind it is still unclear.

There are a few plausible explanations. Interest in tokenized assets, stablecoins, and decentralized finance apps on the XRPL may be pushing people to set up new wallets. Exchange onboarding and automated wallet creation could also be adding to the count.

But more accounts doesn't necessarily mean more users. One person can open several accounts, and automated systems can open many more, so other on-chain indicators are needed to judge real adoption.

XRPScan's history also shows account creation has spiked before, with an all-time high of about 30,600 accounts. The latest jump is well short of that.

The network numbers are growing, but the price paints a different picture.

TradingView data from November 2 shows XRP trading near $1.25, after a long correction from its September and October highs. It is still below several major moving averages, so bearish pressure continues to dominate the technical picture.

Immediate support sits around $1.20–$1.25. If XRP tries to recover, the $1.30-$1.35 region could act as resistance.

Rising account creation alongside falling prices reflects blockchain adoption and market demand, which are not the same thing. Stronger confirmation of growing XRPL adoption would need sustained growth in active addresses, transaction volumes, and general use of the ecosystem.

For now, the 142.4% increase is an encouraging sign of network activity. Whether it turns into real demand for XRP is still an open question.

#5227. HashPack Adds HBAR Tokenized Stock Without LP Reliance

Home » Trendsetter News » HashPack Adds HBAR Tokenized Stock Without LP Reliance

HashPack users can now access tokenized stocks and ETFs through SODAX using HBAR or Hedera’s wrapped USDC version.

HashPack users can now buy tokenized stocks and ETFs through SODAX without relying on liquidity pools on Hedera, according to CEO and co-founder May. Speaking with the host about the wallet’s latest upgrades, she described an integration that lets users pay with HBAR or Hedera USDC while accessing liquidity outside the network.

That distinction matters for larger trades. Assets traded through shallow pools can suffer significant price slippage; May said the SODAX integration avoids depending on locally supplied liquidity to execute purchases.

According to May, buyers receive an HTS token representing a Robinhood stock token issued on Robinhood Chain. She said SODAX maintains the one-to-one relationship, giving users exposure to the underlying asset’s price without requiring another wallet or a manual move to another blockchain.

“You’re not relying on liquidity that exists on the network,” she said. Previously, most assets available to trade through HashPack depended on SaucerSwap pools, apart from token-launch platforms that subsequently created pools there.

May also described dividends as being reinvested into the same stock rather than distributed as cash, qualifying that explanation with “as far as I know.”

The interview did not establish the products’ legal ownership rights, redemption terms or geographic restrictions; details investors would need before treating them as interchangeable with brokerage-held shares.

She sees potential for lending and borrowing against tokenized stocks, although the discussion did not establish that those functions are available inside HashPack.

The stock integration accompanies HashPack’s “Portfolio” redesign, which adds a customizable homepage and bottom-opening navigation dock. May said most users access the wallet on mobile, and its growing collection of swaps, staking options and NFT integrations had made features harder to find.

Enterprise integrations remain a slower prospect. HashPack has ongoing discussions, May said, but nothing particularly exciting to flag for the short term; she suggested developments could emerge over 12 to 24 months.

#5226. Ethereum whale buys $38M as fees hit 2026 high after Binance breach

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Binance breach led to a surge of activity across Ethereum [ETH], pushing daily fees to a 2026 high. This surge resulted in record-breaking daily costs at $47.3 million on the 30th of October.

These costs were higher than the previously reported February cost of $34.5 million by 37.1%. The spike was due to hackers rapidly converting stolen funds into tokens and subsequently executing trades on the network.

The increase in trading activities increased competition for arbitrage and MEV bot traders who seek profit from the opportunity to execute their trades quickly. As such, Ethereum’s volume is far outpacing volumes for other platforms.

This includes BNB Chain and Base, which generated $2.47 million and $2.71 million, respectively.

Gas fees have been increasing toward 253 Gwei on the 29th of October, as demand for block space continues to rise. Whether this increase in activity will be an indication of further stress within the overall market is still unclear.

Although the Binance breach triggered intense trading activity on Ethereum, whales have utilized this volatility to accumulate long-term positions. On the 29th of October, whale 0x9EcA purchased 16,658 ETH using approximately $37.96 million in USDC.

With each purchase averaging $2,279 per token, they executed multiple buys through Uniswap’s [UNI] V2 Dutch Order Reactor in order to facilitate the conversion of USDC to ETH. Each individual buy ranged from 349 ETH to nearly 375 ETH.

This demonstrates sustained accumulation as opposed to simply a large-scale order. Therefore, these purchases may help to support demand for ETH during periods of continued uncertainty.

However, one whale’s purchases alone cannot confirm a broader shift in sentiment or reverse selling pressure.

Even though whales continue to accumulate large amounts of ETH, Ethereum’s price recovery is faced with yet another challenge in the U.S. market, where buying demand remains weak.

The Coinbase Premium index fell to –0.21 on the 29th of October, the lowest levels since February, as ETH prices continued to trade below Binance prices.

Therefore, the extended discount indicates either stronger selling pressure or less buying interest among the U.S. traders, thereby possibly neutralizing any buying pressure exhibited by larger on-chain players.

However, the index has since rebounded toward –0.13, indicating some reduction in that pressure.

Still, the reading remains negative, leaving U.S. demand on uncertain footing. A sustained move above zero would provide stronger evidence of renewed buying interest and improve Ethereum’s recovery prospects.

Ethereum recorded $47.3 million in daily fees after the Binance breach triggered intense trading and MEV activity.

A whale accumulated 16,658 ETH, worth $37.96 million, while negative Coinbase Premium readings exposed persistent weakness in U.S. demand.

#5225. Treasury Sanctions 11 Over North Korean IT Worker Scheme That Moved Millions in Crypto

Treasury Sanctions 11 Over North Korean IT Worker Scheme That Moved Millions in Crypto

The U.S. Treasury Department has sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in North Korean IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the country's weapons programs, the department said on Wednesday.

North Korea uses fake documents, stolen identities and invented personas to place IT workers at legitimate companies, then takes most of their wages, generating hundreds of millions of dollars for its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs, according to Treasury. The networks have used "sophisticated cryptocurrency transactions," money laundering and artificial intelligence tools to move millions of dollars to the regime, it said.

Today, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK’s unlawful weapons of mass…

— Treasury Department (@USTreasury) October 28, 2026

"The North Korean regime continues targeting and exploiting American companies through fraudulent activities conducted by its overseas IT operatives, who weaponize sensitive data and extort businesses for substantial payments," said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Two Russian nationals are among those sanctioned. Vitold Obertas, a Russian intermediary for North Korean financial transactions, has carried out nearly $2 million in crypto conversions since January 2025, plus at least $1.25 million in other currency transactions, for North Korean officials, Treasury said. Ilya Boykov has exchanged and converted the equivalent of $3.5 million in crypto since 2024 for Limited Liability Company Alis, a North Korean IT worker company sanctioned in 2024.

The sanctions listings include two Ethereum and two Tron addresses for Boykov, and one Ethereum and three Tron addresses for Obertas. One Ethereum address appears on both men's entries.

Treasury also sanctioned the First Financial and Technical Development Center, a North Korean-controlled entity based in Vladivostok, Russia, that it said deploys highly trained IT workers who use AI tools and "complex cryptocurrency transfers" to generate revenue. Six Russia-based North Korean IT workers have generated more than $750,000 for the center since 2025, according to Treasury.

Two North Korean nationals who lead Russia-based IT worker delegations were also sanctioned. One of them, Kim Ki Hyok, has transferred nearly $500,000 in crypto for his delegation since 2024, Treasury said.

The action builds on sanctions against a separate North Korean IT worker network in March, and Australia and the European Union have made their own designations this month, according to Treasury.

North Korean IT workers have increasingly targeted crypto projects. In April 2025, Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported that such workers had embedded themselves in crypto projects in the UK, Germany, Portugal and Serbia, including Solana smart contract development, with some operating under as many as 12 fake identities at once.

North Korean hackers have also used long-running deception campaigns against crypto firms. In April, Solana-based exchange Drift Protocol said the attack that drained about $285 million from its platform was a six-month operation by a North Korean state-affiliated group, whose intermediaries met Drift contributors in person and posed as a quantitative trading firm, Decrypt reported.

#5224. Big Week Ahead as XRP Ledger Eyes Cleanup Upgrade

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is set for a significant week ahead as its long-awaited cleanup upgrade heads for mainnet activation this week, bringing a wide-ranging collection of fixes and improvements to the blockchain.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment, a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation, is at the center of attention, with validator support putting it on track for a potential November 4 activation, provided the required voting threshold of 80% is sustained.

The earliest activation date is Nov 4, 2026 at 2:46 PM UTC, with just 2 days left according to the xrpscan countdown timer.

Some tokens on the XRP Ledger are supposed to be stored in accounts approved by their issuer; however, developers have found a few ways around that rule.

Issuers of regulated assets, such as stablecoins or tokenized funds, can require approval before anyone holds their tokens, typically to perform identity checks first.

Four proposed code changes would resolve the remaining exceptions. All four are included in a single network upgrade dubbed fixCleanup3_5_0.

These have not been merged into the XRP Ledger's main software yet. Once they are, fixCleanup3_5_0 requires support from more than 80% of the network's trusted validators for two weeks before being activated.

According to Hussein Zangana (Vet), director of community at XRP Ledger Foundation, there is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability on kernels 4.4+, affecting any unpatched Linux server in the world with an open IPv4 TCP port. For XRP Ledger node and validator operators who run RHEL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK, a fix has already been shipped; they are simply expected to update and reboot.

For those who run Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS Stream, this might not suffice, as they may need to take further steps until a fix is shipped for their distro. They should re-apply the nft rule after a reboot or a flush ruleset reload.
